question: A 55-year-old man with a community-acquired pneumonia is prescribed a fluoroquinolone. Which bacterial target does this drug class primarily act on?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Fluoroquinolones inhibit bacterial type II topoisomerases — DNA gyrase (primary in Gram-negatives) and topoisomerase IV (primary in Gram-positives) — preventing DNA supercoiling and replication.
The 50S subunit is the target of macrolides, chloramphenicol, and clindamycin — not fluoroquinolones.
That is the target of sulfonamides, not fluoroquinolones.

answers.text: Penicillin-binding proteins on the bacterial cell wall

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: PBPs are targeted by beta-lactam antibiotics. Fluoroquinolones have an entirely different intracellular target.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the DNA/Metabolic Pathway Inhibitors section. Fluoroquinolones uniquely target bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV.
Excellent. Fluoroquinolone dual-target inhibition explains why resistance requires mutations in both gyrase and topoisomerase IV genes.
